extracted.intended_audience: researchers and community members who review or request reviews of preprints (particularly early-career researchers and those running or joining reviewing communities)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and platform-level norms for producing and hosting PREreviews on the PREreview/Sciety platform, covering rapid structured reviews, full text reviews (DOI-assigned), identity/pseudonymity options, community conduct, and the PReF descriptors used to describe groups' evaluation activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: increase diversity, equity, transparency in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: PREreview's mission is to bring more equity and transparency to scholarly peer review by supporting and empowering communities of researchers, particularly those at early stages of their career (ECRs) and historically excluded, to review preprints in a process that is rewarding to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform focus implies that reviews and community practices should prioritize inclusion, support for ECRs, and transparent, equitable processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid PREreview (12-question structured form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fill out a rapid PREreview—a structured form of 12 yes/no/not sure/n.a. questions designed to capture the essence of the preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rapid PREreviews are intended to be quick, structured assessments; the binary/ternary answer format is meant to capture key elements succinctly rather than provide long-form critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full PREreview (text review report with DOI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compose a full PREreview—a text review report that upon submission is assigned a DOI via Zenodo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full PREreviews are citable, longer-form reviews. They can be commented on, endorsed via Plaudit.pub, and reported if they violate the Code of Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered-user anonymity/pseudonymity control
rubrics_metrics.description: As a registered user (PREreviewer), you are able to switch between Public and a unique Anonymous Persona for any public action you perform on the platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may choose to reveal or hide their identity on public actions; this is a platform-level feature supporting privacy/pseudonymity while still enabling attribution within the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting PREreviews on preprints (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request a PREreview on any preprint with a registered DOI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both authors and non-authors can request PREreviews (see PReF 'Review requested by' field).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public interaction and commenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Users may comment on others’ full PREreviews; public interaction is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform supports public discussion around full PREreviews; communities can engage openly with reviews and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endorsement via Plaudit.pub
rubrics_metrics.description: Endorse others’ full PREreviews via Plaudit.pub.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plaudit endorsements provide a lightweight signal of appreciation/agreement with a full PREreview; endorsements are part of the public ecosystem around reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting violations of the Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Report others’ full PREreviews as violating our Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is an explicit mechanism for flagging reviews that breach community standards; maintainers pledge a harassment-free environment and ask members to follow the Code of Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Conduct (harassment-free pledge)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the interest of fostering an open and welcoming environment we, as contributors and maintainers, pledge to making participation in our project and our community a harassment-free experience for everyone ... We ask all community members to agree our Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community members are expected to abide by the Code of Conduct; the platform emphasizes inclusion across dimensions (age, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, experience level, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of competing interests at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: We ask all community members to ... disclose any competing interest at the time of PREreview submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors/reviewers should declare competing interests when submitting a PREreview; this disclosure is a community expectation even if group metadata may or may not capture it.

rubrics_metrics.name: PReF: Review requested by (metadata descriptor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review requested by — Authors, Non-authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PReF descriptors are used to describe key elements of a Group's evaluation activities so readers can interpret and compare evaluations; 'Review requested by' indicates who typically initiates the review request.

rubrics_metrics.name: PReF: Reviewer selected by (metadata descriptor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer selected by — Self-nominated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This PReF field communicates how reviewers are chosen for that group's activities (e.g., self-nomination vs. editor-invited).

rubrics_metrics.name: PReF: Public interaction (metadata descriptor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public interaction — Yes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates whether the group's review activities include public discussion/interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: PReF: Inclusion of author response (metadata descriptor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of author response — No.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates whether author responses are incorporated into the group's review record.

rubrics_metrics.name: PReF: Decision (metadata descriptor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision — Other scale or rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes whether the group records a decision or rating and what scale is used (here: 'other' rather than accept/reject).

rubrics_metrics.name: PReF: Review coverage (metadata descriptor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review coverage — Complete paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates whether reviews typically cover the full manuscript or only parts (here: complete paper).

rubrics_metrics.name: PReF: Reviewer identity known to (metadata descriptor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer identity known to — Editor or service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies who (if anyone) knows reviewers' identities beyond the public record; for some groups reviewers are known to editors/services even if public pseudonymity exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: PReF: Competing interests (metadata descriptor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Competing interests — Not included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this group's PReF metadata, competing interests are not included in the group's published metadata fields (even though the platform asks members to disclose them at submission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform openness and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: The PREreview platform is a free and open-source website ... Content is licensed Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International unless otherwise specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews and platform code are intended to be open; full PREreviews receive DOIs and content is generally CC BY 4.0 to permit reuse with attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community formation and group features
rubrics_metrics.description: Join communities of like-minded reviewing groups; Start your own community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform supports organized communities of reviewers and allows groups to define their own practices (which are summarized via PReF descriptors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform role and scope (crowdsourcing preprint reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PREreview platform is a free and open-source website for the crowdsourcing of preprint reviews (PREreviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The model emphasizes rapid, crowd-sourced feedback as complementary to traditional peer review; reviewers and groups contribute to an aggregated set of rapid and full PREreviews alongside preprint PDFs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citable outputs and integration with external services
rubrics_metrics.description: Full PREreviews are assigned a DOI via Zenodo; endorsements via Plaudit.pub; aggregated display alongside preprint PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform integrates with external services for persistence (Zenodo DOIs), endorsement signals (Plaudit), and aggregation to increase discoverability and citability of reviews.
